  * Citation⟨67⟩


#   ⟨68⟩ ALEE: Any-Language Evaluation of Embeddings 
ALEE evaluates text embeddings across a wide range of languages using English-centric minimal pairs. Each English sentence is paired with a set of altered (negative) variants and translated into many languages, so an embedding model can be tested on whether it captures small but meaning-changing differences in any language.
##   ⟨59⟩ Dataset structure 
The dataset has three configurations, each with a single `test` split:
  * `alee_bq275` (864 samples)
  * `alee_f200` (829 samples)
  * `alee_mt61` (818 samples)


###   ⟨60⟩ Fields 
Each row contains (depending on the source dataset) many of the following columns:
  * `eng_Latn`: the original English sentence.
  * `eng_RoleSwap_negative`: English variant with swapped roles.
  * `eng_PolarityNegation_negative`: English variant with added or changed negation.
  * `eng_AntonymRepl_negative`: English variant with an antonym substitution.
  * `eng_HypernymSub_negative`: English variant with a hypernym substitution.
  * Language columns (e.g. `deu_Latn`, `fra_Latn`, `arb_Arab`, `cmn_Hans`, and many more): the translation of the original English sentence into each language. Column names follow the `language_Script` convention.
  * `id`, `uniq_id`, `par_id`: identifiers for the row and its parent paragraph.
  * `domain`, `register`, `level`, `tags`: metadata describing the source text.
  * `orig_text`, `par_comment`: the source sentence and annotation notes.
  * `split`, `newline_next`: split label and formatting flag.


Note: As the generated negatives are validated against NLI, every sample has a subset of the possible negatives. The other columns are left as empty.
##   ⟨61⟩ Usage 
For instructions on how to load the dataset and run the evaluation, see the GitHub repository:
<https://github.com/Andrian0s/any-lang-embed-eval/tree/main>

The negatives generated in ALEE are built on existing multilingual resources. Each configuration draws from a different source. Please cite the source(s) for the configuration you use, alongside ALEE.
